title: Count a category
summary: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category.
introduction: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category. Your task: Add another science row and predict its count.
learningObjectives: Add another science row and predict its count.
Explain the example for count a category

blocks.text: GROUP BY makes one result per category. COUNT counts rows belonging to that category.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'story' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'science' FROM dual)
SELECT kind,COUNT(*) AS total FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`GROUP BY` makes one summary group for each distinct combination of the named grouping values.
`DUAL` lets this Oracle statement return a calculation without an application table.

blocks.text: Science has 1 row and story has 2.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: COUNT(column) ignores NULL in that column. COUNT(*) counts rows.
